extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings, and USPTO OED/disciplinary staff
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for imposing an interim suspension under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25 (including service, respondent rights, filing obligations, publication, and restrictions while suspended).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for interim suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Interim suspension may be ordered under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25 when there is evidence that the practitioner committed serious crimes (e.g., felony convictions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order was predicated on Respondent's conviction for Conspiracy to Commit Securities Fraud (18 U.S.C. § 371) and Securities Fraud (15 U.S.C. §§ 78j(b) and 78ff). The Director may seek interim suspension when such evidence supports that the respondent committed serious crimes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of Notice and Order
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order initiating an interim suspension request must be served (e.g., mailed by certified mail).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order in this case was mailed by certified mail (receipt no. provided) and was delivered to Respondent on July 1, 2019; an earlier attempt on May 17, 2019 was unsuccessful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to respond to Notice and Order
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order provides the respondent an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing the imposition of discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the respondent files a timely response, factual disputes may be presented; failure to respond may lead the Office to conclude there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent fails to file a response to the Notice and Order, the USPTO may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact and proceed with interim suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order states: 'In light of Respondent's failure to file a response, it is hereby determined that there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25 and an interim suspension ... is appropriate.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim suspension effective date
rubrics_metrics.description: The respondent is suspended on an interim basis from practice before the USPTO effective the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order: 'Respondent be suspended on an interim basis ... effective the date of this Final Order.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition for transition period (37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The respondent may be granted limited recognition to practice for a short, specified period solely to facilitate compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this case, limited recognition was granted commencing on the date of the Order and expiring thirty (30) days after the date the Order is signed; explicitly 'for the sole purpose of facilitating Respondent's compliance with the provisions of 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b)'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral to hearing officer for formal disciplinary proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: The Disciplinary Complaint is referred to a hearing officer for conducting a formal disciplinary proceeding pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.25(b)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Complaint (copy attached) shall be referred to a hearing officer as part of the formal process following the interim suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to file written answer to Complaint (37 C.F.R. § 11.36)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must file a written answer to the Complaint within thirty (30) days from the date of the Final Order, addressed to the hearing officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing instructions provided: by mail to Docket Clerk, HUD Office of Hearings and Appeals (address given); if hand-delivered, a separate HUD address is specified. Respondent must also file a PDF version with the hearing office via email and serve a copy on the OED Director by mail (Sydney O. Johnson at given Mail Stop/PO Box).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Notice of Interim Suspension in the Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice of Interim Suspension in the Official Gazette describing the suspension and the convictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample notice includes the respondent's name, location, registration number, the fact of suspension from practice before the USPTO for patent, trademark and other non-patent matters on an interim basis pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.25(b), and cites the underlying criminal convictions and statutory authority (35 U.S.C. § 32; 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.25 and 11.59). It also notes disciplinary decisions are available at the OED FOIA Reading Room URL provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to relevant authorities and USPTO employees
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice of the Final Order to appropriate USPTO employees, interested departments/agencies/courts of the United States, and appropriate state bar authorities where the respondent is known to be a member.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order directs notice be sent to: i) appropriate employees of the USPTO; ii) interested departments, agencies, and courts of the United States; and iii) appropriate authorities of any state in which Respondent is known to be a member of the bar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 (rules governing withdrawal from employment, client notification, and transfer of files upon suspension).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order expressly states: 'Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.' Limited recognition is provided to facilitate such compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from Customer Numbers and PKI certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall dissociate the respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and the public key infrastructure (PKI) certificate associated with those Customer Numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This action severs the respondent's ability to access USPTO electronic services tied to Customer Numbers/PKI while suspended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on obtaining or being added to a USPTO Customer Number while suspended
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for or obtain a USPTO Customer Number, nor shall the respondent have his name added to a USPTO Customer Number, unless and until reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order states these prohibitions explicitly as conditions of the interim suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review does not stay the suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent seeks review of the suspension, such review shall not operate to postpone or hold in abeyance the suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order: 'If Respondent seeks a review of this suspension, any review shall not operate to postpone or otherwise hold in abeyance the suspension.'
